caption_argument_segments: DEMAND PLANNING (NEXT LEVEL) Most people forecast. Few actually plan. Everyone knows the basics: What • When • How Much But real demand planning starts when you ask: Why is demand changing—and what will it cost if I’m w…
1. Not all demand behaves the same Stable → optimize cost Seasonal → manage timing Trend → control scaling risk Irregular → protect with buffers Misclassification = wrong inventory, wrong decisions.
2. There is no universal forecasting model Stop applying one method to all SKUs. Match model to behavior. Segment demand properly. Accept trade-offs (accuracy vs responsiveness)
3. Accuracy is incomplete without direction MAPE tells you how wrong, Bias tells you where you’re leaning High bias = overstock or stockouts Low visibility = unstable decision
4. Forecast = business impact Every number affects: Inventory investment, Service level, Lost sales or excess stock, this is not reporting, this is financial decision-making.

5. Discipline is what creates results Before ordering: Validate trend vs noise. Check real demand drivers. When issues happen: Overstock → check bias Stockout → check missed signals And always: No adjustment without a r…
